threats.title: eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs are recoverable, exposing TLS clients outside browsers to impersonation.
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six of the certificates are for TLS and chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs, and two are for code signing and trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service to clients that still trust the intermediates, including applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle and clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency.

Update curl CA bundle to 2026-10-20 or later
Update Homebrew ca-certificates to 2026-09-25_1 or later
Update Rust rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 or later
Update Ubuntu ca-certificates to 20260816ubuntu0.22.04.1, 20260816ubuntu0.24.04.1, 20260816ubuntu0.26.04.1, 20260816ubuntu0.26.10.1 or later

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports lack request limits
threats.headline: MCP TypeScript SDK servers over HTTP accepted unlimited bodies and batches, enabling unauthenticated denial of service
threats.summary: MCP servers built with the TypeScript SDK and reachable over HTTP put no limit on POST body size or on the number of messages in a JSON-RPC batch. Large requests could exhaust server memory, and one long batch could block the server from serving anyone else. No credentials were needed unless the application authenticates requests before they reach the SDK.
actions: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, cap request body size in a reverse proxy.

threats.title: vLLM SHM multimodal cache allows forged handles to reach pickle
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can forge SHM cache handles to run arbitrary Python in worker processes.
threats.summary: When the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled, vLLM treats an address and monotonic_id pair as authority to read shared memory in the worker. A caller can forge this pair through public HTTP routes so the worker unpickles attacker-staged bytes. This lets an ordinary authenticated inference caller execute arbitrary Python in the worker process, even with insecure serialization disabled.
actions: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.

action_quotes.action: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.
action_quotes.quote: When --mm-processor-cache-type shm is enabled, vLLM's multimodal SHM cache represents a cached item with an address and monotonic_id pair and treats that pair as authority to dereference shared memory in the worker.

who: vLLM deployments using SHM multimodal caching
threats.quote: An ordinary authenticated inference caller can execute arbitrary Python in the worker process on a deployment that uses SHM multimodal caching.

threats.title: vLLM DeepSeek-OCR image validation crashes the engine
threats.headline: A single ordinary PNG can permanently crash vLLM servers running DeepSeek-OCR family models
threats.summary: This trips an assertion in the engine worker that is not contained per request, and the whole process tree shuts down. An unauthenticated chat request under default configuration can take the server down until a manual restart.

threats.title: vLLM out-of-vocabulary token id crashes engine
threats.headline: A single pre-tokenized request with an out-of-range token id can crash vLLM engines serving Llama-2 models.
threats.summary: vLLM's input validation accepts a token id equal to the vocabulary size for models whose vocabulary is an exact multiple of 64, such as the Llama-2 family. At tensor-parallel size 1 the id reaches the embedding lookup out of range and raises a CUDA device-side assert that takes the engine down. Any client that can send pre-tokenized input can trigger it.
threats.quote: At tensor-parallel size 1 the embedding lookup does not mask indices, so the id reaches F.embedding out of range and raises a CUDA device-side assert, which poisons the engine's CUDA context and takes the engine down.

threats.title: vLLM chat template rendering lets one request wedge endpoints
threats.headline: Unbounded Jinja2 chat template rendering in vLLM lets one request or model repo block all chat endpoints.
threats.summary: One short authenticated request can permanently block all chat-style endpoints for every tenant until restart, and a variant can exhaust memory and kill the API server. A malicious model repo carrying a hostile template in its tokenizer config has the same effect on every replica that loads it.
threats.quote: In a multi-tenant deployment this is a cross-tenant denial-of-service from any one tenant.

threats.summary: The MCP Python SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check a token's audience. Patched versions add an opt-in check that stays off unless configured.

items.title: Aggressive local quants need repetition-loop tests before they touch document pipelines
items.connection: Unsloth's 1-bit quant claims 91% top-1 retention, but that check does not measure repetition loops, and Boo Bench's 179 loop-triggering pages plus llama.cpp's fixed reasoning budget make a cheap, predictable loop test for local runs.
items.context: heavy quantization can change generation behavior in ways accuracy checks miss
chain: Firms are tempted to run a 1-bit frontier model locally as the generation step of document extraction.
Top-1 agreement says nothing about repetition loops, which silently corrupt extracted text.
Boo Bench gives 179 pages built to trigger loops, and llama.cpp's budget fix ends reasoning predictably, so loop failures are not confused with runaway thinking.
Teams can pick quant levels by loop rate, not only accuracy, and catch corruption before it reaches ledgers or case files.
items.who: Accounting, audit and claims teams running private extraction; their platform or vendor pays for the testing.
items.versus: Trusting a vendor accuracy number misses a failure mode that does not show up until bad text is already downstream.
items.smallest_test: Run Boo Bench pages through the pipeline with the 1-bit quant and with a higher-precision model; success if the loop counts differ by enough to change which model the team would choose.
items.disconfirm: The 1-bit quant loops no more often than higher-precision runs across the benchmark.

items.context: regulated firms must show change control over who and what modified production code
chain: Every agent edit now carries a link to the conversation that requested it.
A monitoring layer can compare the request with the files touched and flag scope creep, such as auth or billing code edited during a styling task.
Flags feed a second, stricter layer before merge, following the layered pattern OpenAI describes.

items.variable: out-of-scope agent changes caught before merge
items.versus: Plain diff review cannot see intent, and existing code review tools lack a record of what the agent was told.
items.smallest_test: Replay a month of agent-written changes through a simple request-versus-files monitor; success if it flags at least a few changes reviewers agree were out of scope and that ordinary review missed.
items.disconfirm: Out-of-scope edits almost never occur, or the monitor's flags are mostly noise reviewers ignore.

items.title: Kernel agents targeting TileLang could bring expert-grade kernels to chips lacking libraries
items.connection: ForgeKernel's agent matched or beat 18 of 22 expert-library kernels on one GPU type, and TileLang gives it a single high-level target for GPUs, CPUs and other accelerators, so the same loop could produce fast kernels where no expert library exists.
items.context: non-NVIDIA accelerators often trail on hand-tuned kernel libraries
chain: An agent can now tune kernels well enough to beat FlashMLA on prefill, 472 versus 518 microseconds.
Pointing it at TileLang instead of raw CUDA lets one agent loop target several hardware backends.
The biggest gains go to hardware with thin kernel libraries, where there is no expert baseline to match.
Cheaper accelerators become credible for inference, which pressures GPU pricing for serving teams.
items.who: Accelerator vendors and inference providers on non-NVIDIA hardware; vendors would pay to close the library gap.
items.variable: inference cost per million tokens on alternative hardware
items.versus: Hiring kernel experts per chip is slow and scarce, and waiting for vendor libraries leaves performance on the table.
items.smallest_test: Have the agent emit a TileLang prefill kernel for a second hardware type; success if it beats the best available library kernel on that hardware.
items.disconfirm: The agent's wins disappear outside the one GPU type, or its TileLang output cannot compete with existing vendor kernels.

items.lead: Mistral's 1T-parameter image-and-text model can be self-hosted, served and fine-tuned from the first day, and it even fits on one workstation.
items.body: Teams can serve it in vLLM, LoRA fine-tune it in Axolotl, or test it privately on a Mac Studio with Unsloth's 223GB 1-bit quant. That puts frontier-scale work on infrastructure a client controls. Quality has not been independently benchmarked, and the 91% top-1 retention figure is Unsloth's own check.

items.lead: An agent tuned GPU kernels well enough to rival expert libraries.
items.body: OpenBMB's open harness lets an agent optimize kernels. Its fused prefill kernel ran in 472 microseconds against FlashMLA's 518, and it matched or beat 18 of 22 expert-library kernels. That could cut inference cost without hand-written CUDA, but it was one live run on one GPU type, so broad gains are unproven.

items.lead: Large-scale speech recognition can now run offline from open weights.
items.body: NVIDIA's 30B-A4B transcription model is on Hugging Face, which gives a local alternative to hosted transcription APIs. That matters to buyers with privacy or connectivity limits. No word error rates are given, so accuracy against hosted services is unknown.
